title: The explorers come home with maps of the Cape Verde islands, and within the month a colonising expedition sails for them

data.explorer: probably García de Ponte de Sor, who was charting the Cape Verde area from 1409 (not confirmed by a save)
data.colonisation: an expedition sets out in March 1420 (Trent)

title: The Castilians of Zamora rise against the Ṭāʾifa of Liyūn under Eduardo de Avellaneda and proclaim a kingdom of their own. Al-Andalus and all its ṭāʾifas stand with Liyūn

After eighty years as a ṭāʾifa, Balansiyya is taken into the crown: its seventeen towns and some 220,000 people, from Balansiyya, Shāṭiba and Dāniya to al-Qant, Elche and Orihuela, Catalan in speech and nearly all Muslim, become lands of the crown. Its lord Melchior of the house of Orihuela goes to the court of Catalonia

data.lord: Melchior of Orihuela (born 1382), to Catalonia; his heir Frederick, born 1412

title: Angra on Terceira in the Azores becomes a settlement of the crown, the empire's first in those islands: a thousand people, Portuguese, Castilian and Leonese settlers
At Fermoselle, above the gorges of the Duero, the Emperor Ismāʿīl with 4,900 men falls on the 370 rebels of Zamora and destroys them without losing a man

data.note: rebellion battles carry no war score in the game

source: save of 11 August 1420 (the war's battle list)

title: The day after Fermoselle the rising of Zamora is at an end

The world at the annexation of Balansiyya: al-Andalus is third among the powers of the world, behind China and England. In the East three empires have risen: Tīmūr's at Samarqand, fourth in the world with 707 towns; the Ottomans at Constantinople, sixth; and the Mamlūks at Cairo, al-Andalus's ally, ninth

wars: France against Brabant and Metz (from 18 February 1420)
data.rivals: England names al-Andalus among its rivals; Castile names al-Andalus, Morocco and France

title: The Kingdom of Qashtāla falls apart. Its 45 towns in the northern mountains become four petty kingdoms: Galicia under Diego Villamarín (23 towns, from Santiago and A Coruña), Asturias under José Fernando Tuñón (8, from Oviedo), Navarre on the Basque coast under Alfonso Gastón (10, from Bilbao), and what is left of Castile, four towns around Santander, under King Pedro

Navarre.note: the save shows the state Sunni though all its people are Catholic; Trent is correcting this in game (Trent, 4 September 1420)

data.mechanism: no war in the save; Navarre has a truce with Castile from that day. The save doesn't show what broke the kingdom up
data.account: the Kingdom of Castile has collapsed into a series of petty kings clinging to the mountains north of our lands (Trent)
